svg.title: Figure 5-7. Loss scenarios: the driver (C1) (WP-A-05 §5)
svg.desc: Figure 5-7: 6 loss scenario cards for the driver (C1). LS-02 (UCA-04, New finding): The driver corrects with torque below the 100-raw threshold. No override is detected; nothing on screen or in sound changes. Above it, only a grey border. The driver stops correcting, believing the item has yielded. New (sub-threshold case; CC-1, CC-2). LS-03 (UCA-06, Known gap): The driver has used Experimental Mode, or read upstream docs. The driver expects stops at lights; the reference configuration runs Chill Mode. The driver does not brake for the light or the stopped car. User information (WP-O-03) not written. LS-13 (UCA-01, Known gap): The driver engages on a road the item does not handle. Entry needs only a PCM edge and 60 km/h; nothing checks road type, curve radius or glare. The item runs outside what it handles. 60 km/h entry floor implemented (#287) but not verified in the vehicle and without a parent TSR; a speed floor does not see road type (FM-08); staying engaged below it is DQ-402. LS-14 (UCA-02, Known gap): The driver steers against the item and expects that to disengage it. By design steering only overrides; the torque continues as in LS-01. The driver never brakes or cancels. As LS-01. LS-15 (UCA-03, UCA-12, New finding): An EPS temporary fault starts while the driver touches the wheel. No event, or only a silent one; the EPS-fault siren after 1 s is the only cue. The driver reacts late to the silent loss of steering. New: no FMEA cause names the suppressed take-over alert (§6). LS-36 (UCA-07, Known gap): The driver presses the accelerator to pass. The driver sees the grey border and no text, and takes the item to be off. On release the car brakes or accelerates back, unexpected. On-screen override alert and HMI clinic do not exist.
svg.text: How each unsafe control action comes about: the cause, what the controller believes or never learns, and the action on the road.
Steps: 1 the cause · 2 named after the scenario's causal-factor type · 3 the unsafe control action
A light correction the item ignores
UCA-04: Driver applies steering torque below the override threshold while the
item keeps commanding the opposite way, and believes the item has yielded
Expects a stop at the red light
UCA-06: Driver expects the item to stop for a red light, stop sign or stationary
vehicle and does not brake (Chill Mode does not stop for lights)
